questions.q: Gradient boosting scored AUC 0.787 and the logistic regression 0.793. Which model does the capstone choose, and why?
options: Gradient boosting, because it is more complex
Neither; AUC cannot compare models
Whichever trained last
The logistic regression: it scored higher and is simpler to explain, serve and monitor
questions.explain: Pick the simplest model that clears the bar. Here the simple model also scored higher on held-out AUC.

questions.q: A no-code MLflow deployment returned [1, 0] for two customers. Why, and what was the fix in the capstone?
options: The default pyfunc predict returns class labels; a custom scoring script calling predict_proba returns risk scores
The model is broken and must be retrained
Azure ML always returns booleans
The endpoint ignored the input data
questions.explain: The pyfunc flavor calls the pipeline's predict(), which returns labels. To return probabilities, use a custom scoring script (which also requires specifying an environment).

questions.q: What top-level key does the Azure ML online endpoint scoring request use in the Microsoft Learn MLflow example?
options: inputs
features
payload
input_data
questions.explain: Azure ML uses input_data (with columns and data), which differs from MLflow's own serving format, so the swagger contract can be generated.

questions.q: Week 2 showed a PSI of 0.83 on monthly spend, but AUC did not fall. What is the right conclusion?
options: The drift check is useless
Drift is a prompt to investigate; confirm impact on performance with labels when they arrive
The model must be retrained immediately without further checks
AUC proves the data did not change
questions.explain: Input drift does not automatically mean worse predictions. It tells you to look, and labelled outcomes tell you whether performance actually changed.

questions.q: What should you do with a deployed online endpoint when the capstone is finished?
options: Leave it running so it looks active
Rename it
Delete it so its compute stops billing
Switch it to batch mode
questions.explain: A managed online endpoint keeps compute allocated. Delete it (for example with begin_delete) once you no longer need it.
